claims.text: The starting material is a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within the lamellar colonies can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
The nanoscale-precipitate intervention can retain or increase strength.
Nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Obstructing dislocation movement with nanoscale precipitates reduces dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups decreases local stress concentrations near internal boundaries.
Reducing local stress concentrations suppresses microcracking and catastrophic damage during straining.
The proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism improves tensile ductility without compromising strength.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the treated alloy will have improved tensile ductility and retained or increased strength.
The prediction applies at room temperature under standard atmospheric conditions.
The optimal density and distribution of nanoscale precipitates are uncertain.
The effects of the intervention on corrosion resistance and high-temperature strength are uncertain.
